scenes.line1: Can you spot a false positive?
scenes.line2: What if you miss a real effect?
scenes.say: Can you spot a false positive? What if you miss a real effect? Let’s break down hypothesis testing.

scenes.label: Testing
scenes.sub: Check if your data supports a claim about a population.
scenes.say: Hypothesis testing checks if your data really backs up a claim about a population.

scenes.title: P-value Output
scenes.say: A p-value tells you how much evidence you have against the null hypothesis. A small p-value means strong evidence.
Type One error is a false alarm—rejecting the null when it’s actually true. Type Two error is missing the signal—failing to reject when there’s a real effect.

scenes.question: How do you minimize both error types?
scenes.right: Balance significance level and power to minimize both errors.
scenes.say: Here’s a trap: Should you just lower the significance level to minimize errors? Not quite. You need to balance significance and power to keep both error types in check.
